Local prototype · One-page PDF

Keep the review moving.

Working draft · not the public submission

The brief was to make Change Stack easier to use without losing what it can do. I focused on understanding the change, checking its code and keeping my place. A developer explored both versions and pointed out where my first version made that harder. This revision responds to that feedback; it is not a completed usability study.

Keep going through files

My version made each file feel like a separate stop. I changed it to one continuous code stream, with sticky filenames and context that follows the active file. The file tree jumps within that stream. Inspect and Return keep the caller’s reading position. Scrolling never marks a file viewed.

Keep the comparison familiar

I removed compact-Before and made equal-width Split the default. Modified files now show their real deletions and unchanged context. Unified stays available. A 36 px layer strip and 56 px file toolbar leave more room for code; secondary controls sit in Tools.

Make orientation and progress easier to read

Overview is a direct destination with the pinned PR and seven source layer rows. Return to review restores the reading position. One primary count says “Viewed 0 of 52 files.” Seen stays on each summary. Coverage details are in About, with a short notice when content is missing.

Attach the discussion to the right code

Severity and resolution sit together: Major · Resolved. Replies remain in the thread. Range notes attach to a file, commit, side and inclusive line range, including deleted lines. A draft keeps its filename when the reviewer scrolls elsewhere. All notes stay local.

What still needs checking

The local fixture contains all 52 GitHub diffs (+5,722 / −127), checked against the pinned before/after content. Only nine layer assignments are verified. Rate limiting still blocks the other 43, the source comparison base and live Split behavior. Those are release gates; this draft has not replaced the public submission. Summary and thread coverage remains partial. Narrow highlights can hide context, so whole ranges stay available.

The next evidence

Next I’d ask a developer to do the same permission-review task in both versions: explain the checks, inspect the guard, return, and leave a range note. I’d record missed checks, lost position and help needed before making further changes.
